source_metadata.title: New Horizons in Venous Thromboembolism Management: A Narrative Review
source_metadata.scope_note: The governing LiteratureAtom MVP is designed for primary literature. This source is a narrative review; atoms describing underlying studies/guidelines are therefore tagged as secondary reports and remain anchored to this review rather than represented as primary-study findings.

atoms.canonical_statement: The narrative review aims to summarize recent evidence on pharmacologic advances, refinements in anticoagulant therapy, and interventional innovations for VTE and to contextualize key randomized trials, updated guidelines, and emerging therapies for clinical practice.
VTE incidence in high-income countries is estimated at 1–2 per 1000 people.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Incidence rates are estimated at 1–2 per 1000 in high-income countries.

atoms.canonical_statement: Up to 50% of patients with proximal DVT develop post-thrombotic syndrome.
Approximately 3% of patients diagnosed with acute PE progress to chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
Direct medical costs of VTE management in the United States are estimated at $7–10 billion per year.
The 2024 ASH/ISTH pediatric VTE guideline conditionally recommends dabigatran or rivaroxaban over standard-of-care anticoagulants for appropriate pediatric patients.

The 2024 NCCN cancer-associated VTE guidance codifies DOACs as a primary treatment option alongside LMWH and recommends at least 3 months of anticoagulation with continuation while cancer is active or treatment continues.

The 2024 ESAIC peri-operative VTE prophylaxis update emphasizes individualized risk assessment and suggests 28–35 days of prophylaxis after very high-risk procedures such as esophagectomy or pneumonectomy.
D-dimer has poor specificity in advanced age, cancer, and inflammation, leading to false-positive results and unnecessary imaging.
P-selectin and E-selectin have been proposed as VTE biomarkers with potentially higher specificity than d-dimer, but recent findings are mixed and further validation is needed.
A 2024 metabolomic study identified adenosine 3′,5′-diphosphate, glutathione, and adenine as candidate acute-VTE biomarkers, each with an AUC exceeding 0.90.

population.label: Patients with acute VTE in a 2024 observational metabolomic study

atoms.canonical_statement: Many proposed novel VTE biomarkers have not undergone rigorous large prospective clinical validation to establish accuracy and clinical utility.
Modern multidetector CTPA is reported to have sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 98% for PE.

population.label: Patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE

quantitative_result.original_result_text: reported sensitivity of 96%, and specificity of 98%

atoms.canonical_statement: Photon-counting CT has demonstrated radiation dose reductions of approximately 50% while improving image quality and reducing contrast-media requirements.

population.label: Patients undergoing photon-counting CT pulmonary imaging

atoms.canonical_statement: AI-assisted worklist reprioritization has been reported to reduce PE report turnaround time by up to 12 minutes.

population.label: CTPA examinations evaluated in AI-assisted radiology workflow studies

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinical management studies comparing novel VTE diagnostic technologies with usual care are needed before routine adoption.
The COBRRA trial reportedly found significantly less major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding with apixaban than rivaroxaban for acute VTE.
A 2024 network meta-analysis of 17 randomized trials including 6623 patients with active cancer found no significant difference among DOACs for VTE recurrence.

population.label: Patients with active cancer in 17 randomized trials

quantitative_result.original_result_text: 17 RCTs with 6623 patients; no significant difference between the DOACs for VTE recurrence

atoms.canonical_statement: In the 2024 active-cancer meta-analysis, apixaban was associated with lower major bleeding risk than edoxaban and did not increase bleeding compared with parenteral anticoagulants.
API-CAT randomized 1766 patients with cancer-associated thrombosis after at least 6 months of anticoagulation to apixaban 5 mg twice daily or 2.5 mg twice daily for 12 months.

population.label: Patients with cancer-associated thrombosis after at least 6 months of anticoagulation

atoms.canonical_statement: API-CAT found reduced-dose apixaban non-inferior to full-dose apixaban for recurrent VTE prevention and associated with less major bleeding during extended treatment.
A 2024 meta-analysis encompassing 23 cohort studies and randomized trials and 465,673 patients with CKD found DOACs associated with significantly lower major bleeding and mortality than VKAs.

population.label: Patients with chronic kidney disease in 23 cohort studies and randomized trials

quantitative_result.original_result_text: 23 cohort studies and randomized trials and 465,673 patients with CKD

atoms.canonical_statement: The review interprets the CKD evidence as reassuring for DOAC use, especially apixaban, in severe renal impairment while emphasizing that additional evidence is needed.
During pregnancy, LMWH remains the anticoagulant of choice; UFH is used in severe renal dysfunction, and VKAs and DOACs are avoided because of placental transfer and potential fetal effects.
During breastfeeding, LMWH and VKAs are considered safe, whereas DOACs are generally not recommended because they are excreted into breast milk and infant-safety data are insufficient.
Factor XI is presented as an anticoagulant target because it contributes to thrombus amplification and stabilization while having a comparatively modest role in physiologic hemostasis.
In a phase 2 total-knee-arthroplasty trial, a single postoperative intravenous dose of abelacimab 75 mg or 150 mg reduced VTE by approximately 80% versus enoxaparin 40 mg, with no observed bleeding.

exposures.details: single postoperative dose; 75 mg or 150 mg

atoms.canonical_statement: In AZALEA-TIMI 71, abelacimab 150 mg reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding by 67% versus rivaroxaban in atrial fibrillation.

population.label: Patients with atrial fibrillation in AZALEA-TIMI 71

concept.text: Major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding

atoms.canonical_statement: In AZALEA-TIMI 71, abelacimab 150 mg reduced major bleeding by 74% versus rivaroxaban.

population.label: Patients with atrial fibrillation in AZALEA-TIMI 71

atoms.canonical_statement: The review characterizes factor XI(a) inhibitors as a potentially major anticoagulation paradigm shift because of their apparently favorable bleeding profile, while noting that phase 3 efficacy testing remains essential.
Table 1 reports osocimab as non-inferior to enoxaparin/apixaban for post-knee-arthroplasty VTE prevention in FOXTROT.
Table 1 reports that DS1040 was safe in a phase 1b PE trial but did not significantly reduce thrombus burden in intermediate-risk PE.
Systemic thrombolysis in intermediate-risk PE is associated with intracranial hemorrhage rates of approximately 3–4%, supporting guideline preference for anticoagulation in most such patients.
PEERLESS enrolled 550 patients with intermediate-risk PE and randomized large-bore mechanical thrombectomy versus catheter-directed thrombolysis.
In PEERLESS, post-procedural ICU admission occurred in 41.6% of patients receiving large-bore mechanical thrombectomy versus 98.6% receiving catheter-directed thrombolysis.

population.label: Patients with intermediate-risk PE in PEERLESS

atoms.canonical_statement: In PEERLESS, clinical deterioration or rescue therapy occurred in 1.8% with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy versus 5.4% with catheter-directed thrombolysis.

population.label: Patients with intermediate-risk PE in PEERLESS

atoms.canonical_statement: The PEERLESS primary endpoint was criticized for including ICU utilization because CDT patients are almost universally treated in the ICU; the review states that excluding this component would remove statistical significance from the primary outcome.

HI-PEITHO is designed to compare ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis plus standard anticoagulation with anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high-risk PE, using a 7-day composite of PE-related death, cardiorespiratory decompensation, or recurrent PE as the primary outcome.
ATTRACT did not show that adding catheter-directed thrombolysis to anticoagulation reduced overall post-thrombotic syndrome incidence in most patients with proximal DVT.
CAVA did not demonstrate a reduction in post-thrombotic syndrome with catheter-directed thrombolysis versus anticoagulation alone in iliofemoral DVT.

ATTRACT subgroup analysis suggested that patients with iliofemoral DVT may have a greater reduction in moderate-to-severe post-thrombotic syndrome with catheter-directed thrombolysis than with anticoagulation alone.

population.label: Patients with iliofemoral DVT in ATTRACT subgroup analysis

quantitative_result.original_result_text: may benefit from a greater reduction in moderate-severe PTS incidence

atoms.canonical_statement: A 2025 comparison of six cancer-associated thrombosis risk models found poor-to-modest predictive performance across all models.
The Cleveland Clinic Bleeding Model incorporates 16 factors and is reported to discriminate in-hospital bleeding better than the IMPROVE bleeding risk model.
A 2024 machine-learning VTE model using a “fuzzy population” approach achieved higher specificity with equivalent sensitivity compared with the Padua score.

The 2024 TRiP(cast) implementation trial used a trauma-, immobilization-, and patient-characteristic-based score to identify low-risk lower-limb-trauma patients who could safely avoid prophylactic anticoagulation.

The review proposes a future two-step prophylaxis strategy: first exclude low-risk patients with a validated score, then assess individualized thrombosis-versus-bleeding net clinical benefit among those remaining.
High-quality evidence remains limited for VTE management in populations often excluded from major trials, including severe obesity, severe renal or hepatic failure, and pregnancy.
The review identifies prevention and treatment of chronic VTE sequelae, including post-thrombotic syndrome and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, as persistent unmet needs.

The review concludes that VTE management is moving toward personalized prevention and treatment integrating clinical, molecular, imaging, and AI-derived information, alongside emerging factor XI(a) inhibitors and better-defined catheter-based therapy.
The authors report that the review received no external funding.
Wassim Bedrouni and Mahdi Bedrouni report no relevant conflicts of interest, and James Douketis reports no conflicts of interest within the past 24 months.
The authors state that ChatGPT version 5 was used to reformat the reference list and that they reviewed and edited the output.
